sessions.name: connect: subscription gate, post-subscription handshake, startup with a SupportFunction reply (R10M profile)

steps.note: Connected only now. 02 00 is the CCCD "enable indications" value.
Post-subscription handshake: device name request, written before anything else.
setTime at the session instant (local wall clock).
Synthetic 14-byte SupportFunction bitmap: byte 0 bit 0 (blood pressure), byte 8 bit 0 (temperature). Adds TEMPERATURE monitor 01 20 and history types 08 and 1e.
History starts with sport. "05 02 00" = no data: advance without an ack.
Temperature monitor, queued by the 02 01 reply behind the already-queued startup batch.
Live status asked once more after the startup history walk.

sessions.note: Assembled from several Kotlin tests; the wire order assumes Lumen's FIFO write queue (the whole startup batch and the first history query are queued before any reply is handled). The ring's replies to 02 03, 01 00, 02 07 and the settings writes are not modelled (no Kotlin vector). Notifications are put on the stream channel as the Kotlin tests do; which channel the real ring answers each command on is unverified.

sessions.name: spot heart rate ending in 04 0e

steps.note: Start accepted (status 00).
Every 04 push is acknowledged with 04 <key> 00.
The ring ends the measurement itself (mode 00, status 01 = success).
The app always writes the stop, even after the ring ended it.

sessions.note: Synthetic: the frames are the decoder/driver test vectors stitched together. On hardware the ring ended a spot HR at about 35 s; the 45 s ceiling only applies when 04 0e never comes. Lumen settles the value from the samples it collected (the vendor app re-syncs history instead).

sessions.name: spot SpO2 ending in 04 0e
sessions.note: Raised SpO2 ceiling: 75 s (default 60). Five hardware captures ended with 04 0e at about 63 s.

steps.note: A stop records no started mode, so its reply can never be a refusal.
